mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% in the month before decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 4% months, or the IC > 0.05 over a 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 jobs coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger labor demand is interpreted as a growth signal by markets.
failure_condition: Over 3 consecutive months with PAYEMS > 10,000 increases, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy HOUST below their 5-week moving averages triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates softening demand.
failure_condition: IC < -0.1 over a 6-month window when both proxies cross their MA thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% for three consecutive months is interpreted as a supply-side expansion that supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 10 such 3-month windows, 20-day returns are not significantly positive (IC <= 0.0).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months during a low-inflation regime, markets anticipate lower policy rates, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for 2 consecutive months and regime: low inflation
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in >40% of such UNRATE < 4% periods (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in unemployment (PAYEMS) below 4% triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate a risk-off reaction to sudden labor market tightening.
failure_condition: Over 8 such episodes, 5-day returns are not negative (IC > 0.0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both consumer confidence proxy HOUST and retail sales (not available in catalog - so use RSAFS as proxy for retail) suggest weakening demand, resulting in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: IC > 0.1 when both proxies cross their respective MA thresholds over a 4-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where both inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are rising in tandem, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as higher-for-longer inflation is offset by expectations of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rising trend and FEDFUNDS rising trend
regime_hint: coordinated inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: Over 5 such regime-identified windows, 60-day returns are not positive (IC <= 0.0).
